title: Static GK
summary: Books and authors, sports, awards, important days, national symbols and firsts, and organisations with their headquarters, currencies and parliaments. These are facts that do not change year to year and add up to 2–4 GA questions in almost every shift. Learn them as tables and review often.

tricks.title: Booker ladder — "Rushdie 81, Roy 97, Desai 06, Adiga 08"
tricks.body: Four India-connected Booker winners in order: **Midnight's Children → God of Small Things → Inheritance of Loss → White Tiger**. **Geetanjali Shree (2022)** won the **International** Booker (for translated fiction).

example.q: Who wrote 'The White Tiger', the 2008 Booker winner?

tricks.title: Sports book hooks
tricks.body: **Sunny** Days = **Sunil** Gavaskar · **Race** of My Life = Milkha (the 'Flying Sikh' raced) · **Unbreakable** = Mary Kom (boxer) · **Ace** = Sania (tennis ace) · **Test** of My Life = Yuvraj (cancer battle).

mistakes: *Vande Mataram* is from *Anandamath* (Bankim), **not** from Tagore's works — Tagore wrote *Jana Gana Mana*.
*Unto This Last* was written by **John Ruskin**; Gandhi only paraphrased it into Gujarati as *Sarvodaya*.
*The Discovery of India* was written by **Nehru** in Ahmednagar Fort jail (1942–46).

subtopics.title: Sports: Trophies, Terms, Players & Venues
subtopics.concept:
**Trophy → sport**

| Trophy / Cup | Sport |
|---|---|
| Ranji, Duleep, Irani, Deodhar, Vijay Hazare | **Cricket** |
| Santosh Trophy, Subroto Cup (schools), I-League | **Football** |
| Beighton Cup, Aga Khan Cup, Dhyan Chand Trophy | **Hockey** |
| **Thomas Cup** (men), **Uber Cup** (women), Sudirman Cup (mixed) | **Badminton** |
| **Davis Cup** (men), Billie Jean King Cup (women) | **Tennis** |
| Ryder Cup, Walker Cup | Golf |
| Stanley Cup | Ice hockey |
| Wightman Cup | Tennis (women, UK–USA, discontinued) |

**Players per side**

| 5 | 6 | 7 | 9 | 11 | 15 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Basketball | Volleyball, ice hockey | Kabaddi, netball, water polo, handball | Kho-kho (in field), baseball | Cricket, football, hockey | Rugby union |

Polo = 4 per side.

**Terms → sport**: *Googly, LBW, maiden over* → cricket · *Bully, penalty corner* → hockey · *Love, deuce, ace* → tennis · *Checkmate, castling, en passant* → chess · *Smash, drop shot* → badminton · *Birdie, bogey, caddie* → golf · *Raid, bonus line* → kabaddi · *Punch, knock-out, uppercut* → boxing.

**Grand Slam surfaces:** Australian Open (hard, Jan) · **French Open / Roland Garros (clay)** · **Wimbledon (grass)** · US Open (hard, Flushing Meadows).

**Olympics essentials**
- Paris **2024** (India: 6 medals — Neeraj Chopra silver; **Manu Bhaker** two bronzes, the first Indian after independence to win two medals at one Games).
- Los Angeles **2028**, Brisbane **2032**.
- **Abhinav Bindra** — India's first individual Olympic gold (**Beijing 2008**, 10 m air rifle).
- **Neeraj Chopra** — javelin gold, Tokyo 2020 (India's first in athletics).
- Olympic rings: 5 (blue, yellow, black, green, red) = 5 continents.

**Indian stadiums:** Eden Gardens (Kolkata) · Narendra Modi Stadium (Motera, Ahmedabad — world's largest cricket stadium) · Wankhede (Mumbai) · Chepauk / M.A. Chidambaram (Chennai) · Salt Lake / Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan (Kolkata, football) · Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium (Delhi, hockey).

tricks.title: Badminton cups — "Thomas the man, Uber the woman"
tricks.body: **Thomas** Cup = men's team, **Uber** Cup = women's team, **Sudirman** = mixed. Tennis: **D**avis = **D**udes (men), **B**illie Jean King = women.

example.q: India won the Thomas Cup for the first time in 2022. The sport is —

tricks.title: Team size — "Basket 5, Volley 6, Kabaddi 7"
tricks.body: Count up: basketball **5**, volleyball **6**, kabaddi **7**; then cricket/football/hockey **11**.

mistakes: Santosh Trophy is **football**; Ranji Trophy is **cricket**.
Roland Garros is **clay**; Wimbledon is the only Grand Slam on **grass**.
Abhinav Bindra won India's first **individual** gold; India had team golds in hockey much earlier (from 1928).

subtopics.title: Awards & Honours
subtopics.concept:
| Award | Started | Field | First / key facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Bharat Ratna** | **1954** | Highest civilian honour | First: **C. Rajagopalachari, S. Radhakrishnan, C.V. Raman** (1954). First woman: **Indira Gandhi (1971)**. First sportsperson: **Sachin Tendulkar (2014)**. First non-Indian: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (1987); Nelson Mandela (1990). Normally max **3 per year** |
| Padma Vibhushan / Bhushan / Shri | 1954 | 2nd / 3rd / 4th civilian honours | Announced on Republic Day eve |
| **Param Vir Chakra** | 1950 | Highest wartime gallantry | First: **Maj. Somnath Sharma** (1947, posthumous) |
| Ashoka Chakra | 1952 | Highest peacetime gallantry | |
| **Jnanpith** | **1965** | Highest literary award (Indian languages) | First: **G. Sankara Kurup** (Malayalam, *Odakkuzhal*) |
| Sahitya Akademi Award | 1955 | Literature (24 languages) | |
| **Dadasaheb Phalke** | **1969** | Lifetime contribution to cinema | First: **Devika Rani** |
| **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna** | 1991–92 | Highest sports honour | Renamed from Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna in **2021**; first winner **Viswanathan Anand** |
| **Arjuna Award** | 1961 | Sportspersons | |
| **Dronacharya Award** | 1985 | Sports **coaches** | |
| Dhyan Chand Award | 2002 | Lifetime achievement in sport | |

**Indian Nobel laureates**

| Year | Laureate | Field |
|---|---|---|
| 1913 | **Rabindranath Tagore** | Literature (first Asian) |
| 1930 | **C.V. Raman** | Physics (Raman effect) |
| 1979 | **Mother Teresa** | Peace |
| 1998 | **Amartya Sen** | Economics (welfare economics) |
| 2014 | **Kailash Satyarthi** (with Malala Yousafzai) | Peace |

**International awards by field:** Pulitzer → journalism & literature (USA) · Booker → English fiction · Oscar (Academy Award) → film · Grammy → music · Pritzker → architecture · Abel Prize & Fields Medal → mathematics · Kalinga Prize → popularising science (UNESCO).

example.q: Which of the following was NOT among the first Bharat Ratna recipients in 1954? (a) C.V. Raman (b) S. Radhakrishnan (c) Jawaharlal Nehru (d) C. Rajagopalachari

tricks.title: Award decade ladder
tricks.body: **50s** Bharat Ratna (54) → **60s** Arjuna (61), Jnanpith (65), Phalke (69) → **80s** Dronacharya (85) → **90s** Khel Ratna (91–92).

mistakes: Dronacharya is for **coaches**; Arjuna is for **players**.
The first Phalke awardee was **Devika Rani**, not Prithviraj Kapoor (he got it posthumously in 1971).
Khel Ratna was **renamed** after Major Dhyan Chand in 2021; the separate *Dhyan Chand Award* (lifetime) is a different award.

**National days (India)**

| Date | Day | Why |
|---|---|---|

| 15 Jan | Army Day | K.M. Cariappa took over as C-in-C (1949) |
| 25 Jan | National Voters' Day | ECI founded 25 Jan 1950 |

| **15 Sep** | **Engineers' Day** | **M. Visvesvaraya** |
| 8 Oct | Air Force Day | IAF formed 1932 |
| 31 Oct | National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas) | Sardar Patel |
| 14 Nov | Children's Day | Nehru |
| 26 Nov | **Constitution Day** (Samvidhan Divas) | Constitution adopted 1949 |
| 4 Dec | Navy Day | Operation Trident (1971) |
| **22 Dec** | **National Mathematics Day** | **Srinivasa Ramanujan** |
| 23 Dec | Kisan Diwas | Chaudhary Charan Singh |
| 25 Dec | Good Governance Day | A.B. Vajpayee |

**International days**

| Date | Day |
|---|---|

| 22 Mar | World Water Day |
| 7 Apr | World Health Day (WHO founded 1948) |
| 22 Apr | Earth Day |
| **21 Jun** | **International Day of Yoga** (from 2015) |

tricks.title: Birthday days — pair the person
tricks.body: 12 Jan **Vivekananda** → youth · 29 Aug **Dhyan Chand** → sports · 5 Sep **Radhakrishnan** → teachers · 15 Sep **Visvesvaraya** → engineers · 14 Nov **Nehru** → children · 22 Dec **Ramanujan** → maths.

tricks.title: Two 'Feb–Nov' science/constitution anchors
tricks.body: **28 Feb** = Raman effect (Science Day). **26 Nov** = Constitution adopted (26 Jan = enforced → Republic Day).

mistakes: Constitution Day is **26 November** (adoption); Republic Day is 26 January (enforcement).
National Science Day marks the **discovery** of the Raman effect (1928), not Raman's birthday (7 Nov).
Engineers' Day (15 Sep) is Visvesvaraya's birthday; Teachers' Day (5 Sep) is Radhakrishnan's.

subtopics.title: National Symbols & Firsts
subtopics.concept:
**National symbols**

| Symbol | Details |
|---|---|
| National flag | Designed by **Pingali Venkayya**; ratio **3 : 2**; Ashoka Chakra in navy blue with **24 spokes**; adopted 22 July 1947 |
| National emblem | From the **Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath**; adopted 26 Jan 1950; motto ***Satyameva Jayate*** from the **Mundaka Upanishad** |
| National anthem | *Jana Gana Mana* (Tagore); adopted **24 Jan 1950**; full version **52 seconds** |
| National song | *Vande Mataram* (Bankim, *Anandamath*) |
| Animal / bird / flower | **Tiger** (1973) / **Peacock** / **Lotus** |
| Tree / fruit | **Banyan** / Mango |
| Aquatic animal | **Gangetic river dolphin** (2009) |
| Heritage animal | Elephant (2010) |
| National river | Ganga (2008) |

| Chief Justice of India | H.J. Kania |
| Chief Election Commissioner | Sukumar Sen |

| Woman President | Pratibha Patil (2007) |

| Woman IPS officer | Kiran Bedi (1972) |
| Woman Supreme Court judge | **M. Fathima Beevi** (1989) |
| Woman Lok Sabha Speaker | Meira Kumar (2009) |
| Indian in space | **Rakesh Sharma** (1984, Soyuz T-11) |

example.q: Who was India's first woman Chief Minister?

tricks.title: Flag numbers — "3:2 and 24"
tricks.body: Length : width = **3 : 2**; chakra spokes = **24**; designer = **Pingali** Venkayya.

mistakes: *Satyameva Jayate* is from the **Mundaka Upanishad**, not the Rigveda.
The national aquatic animal is the **Gangetic dolphin**, not the whale shark.
The first Governor-General of independent India was **Mountbatten**; the first (and last) **Indian** GG was Rajagopalachari.

tricks.title: Geneva vs Rome vs Nairobi
tricks.body: **Geneva** = health, trade, labour (WHO, WTO, ILO). **Rome** = food (FAO, WFP, IFAD). **Nairobi** = environment (UNEP) — the only major UN HQ in Africa/Global South.

example.q: The headquarters of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) is in —

tricks.title: Neighbour currencies — "Taka, Ngul, Kyat"
tricks.body: East side of India: Bangladesh **Taka**, Bhutan **Ngultrum**, Myanmar **Kyat**. Nepal, Sri Lanka and Pakistan use the **rupee**.

mistakes: Japan's parliament is the **Diet**; Israel's is the **Knesset**.
Australia's capital is **Canberra**, not Sydney; Canada's is **Ottawa**, not Toronto.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: "Who wrote…" or "…is the author of" with four names.
pyqPatterns.approach: Classics and freedom-era books are asked most, then sports autobiographies. Use the Booker ladder for novels.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: A cup or trophy name, a sports term, or "how many players".

pyqPatterns.approach: RRR for Bharat Ratna 1954; Devika Rani for Phalke; G. Sankara Kurup for Jnanpith; Dronacharya = coaches.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: A national or international day with dates (or the person it honours).
pyqPatterns.approach: Tie each date to a birthday or founding event (Vivekananda, Dhyan Chand, Ramanujan, Raman effect).
Group HQs by city (Geneva–Rome–Nairobi–Vienna); neighbour currencies by direction.

solvedExamples.q: Which of the following pairs of book and author is **NOT** correctly matched?
options: India Wins Freedom — Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
The Discovery of India — Jawaharlal Nehru
solvedExamples.solution: *Hind Swaraj* (1909) was written by **M.K. Gandhi** on board a ship from London to South Africa. Tilak's famous works are *Gita Rahasya* and *The Arctic Home in the Vedas*. The other pairs are correct.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Hind Swaraj = Gandhi's first manifesto; Tilak = Gita Rahasya.

solvedExamples.q: How many players does each side have on court in a game of **volleyball**?
solvedExamples.solution: Volleyball is played **6-a-side**. Basketball has 5, kabaddi 7 and baseball/kho-kho 9.

solvedExamples.q: Who was the first recipient of the **Dadasaheb Phalke Award**, instituted in 1969?
solvedExamples.solution: Actress **Devika Rani** ('First Lady of Indian Cinema') received the first Phalke Award for 1969. Prithviraj Kapoor received it posthumously (1971), Raj Kapoor in 1987 and Satyajit Ray in 1984.
solvedExamples.shortcut: First Phalke = the First Lady of Indian cinema.

solvedExamples.q:
Match the organisations with their headquarters and choose the correct option.

A. UNESCO  B. UNEP  C. IAEA

1. Vienna  2. Paris  3. Nairobi
solvedExamples.solution: **UNESCO – Paris**, **UNEP – Nairobi**, **IAEA – Vienna** (also home to OPEC).
solvedExamples.shortcut: Fix UNESCO = Paris first — only option (a) and (c) have A-2; then UNEP = Nairobi settles it.

practice.solution: ***Godan*** (1936), Premchand's last completed novel, tells the story of the poor farmer Hori. Premchand also wrote *Gaban* and *Nirmala*.

practice.q: ***The God of Small Things***, winner of the 1997 Booker Prize, was written by —
practice.solution: **Arundhati Roy** won the Booker in **1997** for this Kerala-set debut novel. Kiran Desai won in 2006 for *The Inheritance of Loss*.

practice.q: ***Playing It My Way*** is the autobiography of —
practice.solution: ***Playing It My Way*** (2014) is **Sachin Tendulkar**'s autobiography, written with Boria Majumdar.
practice.shortcut: Sachin — 'my way' of playing for 24 years.

practice.q: ***Poverty and Un-British Rule in India***, which set out the 'drain of wealth' theory, was written by —
practice.solution: **Dadabhai Naoroji**, the 'Grand Old Man of India', published this book in 1901. R.C. Dutt wrote *The Economic History of India*.
The **Santosh Trophy** is India's national football championship for state teams, first held in 1941. The Ranji Trophy is its cricket counterpart.

practice.q: The **Uber Cup** is a world team championship for —
practice.solution: The **Uber Cup** is the women's world team badminton championship. The **Thomas Cup** is its men's version.

practice.q: The terms '**bully**' and '**penalty corner**' are associated with —
practice.solution: Both terms belong to **field hockey** — a bully restarts play between two players, and a penalty corner is awarded for defensive fouls inside the circle.
practice.shortcut: Penalty **corner** + bully = hockey (football has corner kicks, not penalty corners).

practice.q: Which Grand Slam tennis tournament is played on **clay courts**?
practice.solution: The **French Open** at Roland Garros, Paris is the only Grand Slam on **clay**. Wimbledon is on grass; the Australian and US Opens are on hard courts.

practice.q: Which shooter won India's **first individual Olympic gold medal**?
practice.solution: **Abhinav Bindra** won the **10 m air rifle** gold at **Beijing 2008**. Rathore won silver in 2004 (double trap); Narang and Vijay Kumar won medals in 2012.

practice.q: Which of the following received the **Bharat Ratna in 1954**, the first year of the award?
practice.solution: The 1954 recipients were **C. Rajagopalachari, S. Radhakrishnan and C.V. Raman**. Nehru got it in 1955; Ambedkar and Patel received it posthumously in 1990 and 1991.

practice.q: The **Dronacharya Award** is given for excellence in —
practice.solution: Instituted in **1985**, the Dronacharya Award honours **sports coaches**. The Arjuna Award is for sportspersons.
practice.shortcut: Drona was the guru (coach) of Arjuna — coach vs player.

practice.q: The first **Jnanpith Award** (1965) went to G. Sankara Kurup, who wrote in —
practice.solution: **G. Sankara Kurup** received the first Jnanpith for his **Malayalam** poetry collection *Odakkuzhal* ('The Bamboo Flute').

practice.q: **National Science Day** is celebrated in India on —
practice.solution: **28 February** marks C.V. Raman's discovery of the **Raman effect** in 1928. 7 November is Raman's birthday; 11 May is National Technology Day (Pokhran-II, 1998); 15 September is Engineers' Day.
practice.shortcut: Science Day = discovery date, not birthday.

practice.q: **National Sports Day** (29 August) is observed on the birth anniversary of —
practice.solution: Hockey wizard **Major Dhyan Chand** was born on 29 August 1905. The Khel Ratna is also named after him (since 2021).

practice.q: Who was the **first woman Governor** of an Indian state?
practice.solution: **Sarojini Naidu** became Governor of the United Provinces (now UP) in 1947. Sucheta Kriplani was the first woman Chief Minister (UP, 1963). Her daughter Padmaja Naidu later governed West Bengal.

practice.q: The motto '**Satyameva Jayate**' on India's national emblem is taken from the —
practice.solution: The words come from the **Mundaka Upanishad** ('Truth alone triumphs'). The emblem itself is adapted from Ashoka's Lion Capital at Sarnath.
Bhutan's currency is the **Ngultrum**, pegged at par with the Indian rupee. Taka = Bangladesh, Kyat = Myanmar, Rupiah = Indonesia.

practice.q: The headquarters of the **International Labour Organization (ILO)** is in —
practice.solution: The ILO, founded in **1919**, is based in **Geneva**, along with WHO and WTO.
The **Knesset** is Israel's unicameral legislature in Jerusalem. Iran – Majlis, Japan – Diet, Norway – Storting.
